question_text: Name a microbe used for statin production. How do statins lower blood cholesterol level?

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.48, printed question 137. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK NOTE: the guide calls Monascus purpureus a yeast, following NCERT. It is in fact a filamentous FUNGUS, the red mould of red yeast rice. NCERT's wording is kept and the biology is noted.

insider_note: The mechanism is the second mark and it is one phrase: competitive inhibition of the enzyme that makes cholesterol.

steps.why: Statins were found as a natural product of a mould long before anyone set out to design a cholesterol drug.
common_mistakes: Naming Penicillium. Penicillium makes PENICILLIN; Monascus purpureus makes statins.
Spelling it Monascus purpurus. The species is purpureus.

steps.label: How statins work
steps.margin_note: Name competitive inhibition and say what is blocked. This is the mark.

lines.text: They block the enzyme that makes cholesterol

lines: Statins lower blood cholesterol by COMPETITIVELY
INHIBITING the enzyme responsible for the
Because the statin resembles the enzyme's own
substrate, it occupies the active site and the
Less cholesterol is made, so the blood level falls.
steps.why: Statins are a real example of the competitive inhibition defined in the enzymes chapter, which is why the two topics are worth reading together.
common_mistakes: Saying statins destroy cholesterol already in the blood. They stop it being MADE.
Leaving out 'competitively'. That word names the mechanism: the statin competes with the substrate for the active site.
steps.memory_tip: It sits in the enzyme's seat, so nothing gets made.
